title: What If You Stopped Eating for a Whole Year?

scenes.text: What if you stopped eating for a whole year? One man did. The ending is the strange part.
In 1965, a Scottish patient in a Dundee hospital started a fast under doctors' supervision. He wanted to lose weight.
He lived on tea, coffee, soda water and vitamin supplements. Regular blood tests checked that he really wasn't eating.
The fast lasted 382 days. He lost well over 120 kilograms, and a Guinness record was set.
His first meal was a boiled egg, bread and butter, and coffee. Five years later, he'd kept almost all the weight off.
But this was under constant medical care. Fasting without it can strain the heart, and people have died trying.

description:
What if you stopped eating for a whole year?
In 1965 a Scottish patient fasted for 382 days under medical supervision, living on tea, coffee, water and vitamins. It remains the longest fast on record, and doctors warn it is not safe alone.
